newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei end sharply off,damaged by BOJ remark.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei end sharply off,damaged by BOJ remark.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei stock index futures tumbled to a weak close well below the key 20,000 level on Wednesday, jolted by comments which raised the spectre of a rise in Japan's official discount rate.

Dealers said the market's uptrend had been damaged by Bank of Japan (BOJ) deputy governor Toshihiko Fukui's comment that the central bank was mulling the right timing to raise its discount rate, at which it lends to commercial banks.
The lead Nikkei 225 June contract fell easily through the 20,000 points level following the comment and ended 515 points lower at 19,830, after medium-term support at 19,900 gave way.
Market turnover was a reasonably healthy 17,650 lots despite a public holiday in Singapore.
"The 19,750 support level has held but it'll take some time to climb back above 20,000. I think we'll go sideways between 19,500 and 20,000 for a while," a trader with a local institution said.

He said the market had been taken completely off guard by the BOJ comments, particularly after the U.S. Federal Reserve decided to leave short-term rates unchanged at its policy-making meeting on Tuesday.
"The Fed didn't do anything and Japan is still thinking of tightening. That's why the Nikkei gave way," he said.
The Fed's move to leave rates intact was widely seen as removing any immediate pressure on the BOJ to hike rates, especially given the yen's recent hefty gains versus the dollar.
On Taiwan futures, the May MSCI index contract ended at 344.7 against its opening 344.5 on volume of 699 lots.
